title: Whole-counit substitution and scalar normalization for realized operations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L\subset M$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, allowing equality, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_F$, uniformizers $\varpi_F$, and $A_{F,n}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes have $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites put $R_{F,X}=\lim_n(A_{F,n})_X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $\mathscr S_F(X)$ for the abelian category of strict quotient-module systems with quotient-linear transitions, $\mathcal R_{F,X}$ for derived reduction and $\mathcal L_{F,X}=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for realization [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A system $C$ is normalized when $C_m\otimes^L_{A_{F,m}}A_{F,n}\to C_n$ is an isomorphism for $m\geq n$ [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

Use the whole-system pullbacks $U_{f,F}$, scalar changes $S_{L/E,X}$ and their specified comparison maps [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems], and the completed pullbacks $\widehat U_{f,F}=Lf_F^*$ and scalar extensions $\widehat S_{L/E,X}=T_{L/E,X}$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

Supply normalized realization models as defined in [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], with whole-system counit $e:\mathcal R\mathcal L\to1$ induced from the K-injective-normalized constant-tower/limit counit $\epsilon$. Let $C,D\in D(\mathscr S_E(Y))$ be normalized systems whose realizations are in $D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and restrict every expression below to systems with constructible-complete intermediate realizations. For a primitive whole-system operation $O$ (a pullback or scalar change), write $\widehat O$ for the corresponding completed operation, and $b_{O,K}:\widehat OK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LO\mathcal RK$ for its prescribed model isomorphism. Define
$$r_{O,C}=\mathcal L(O(e_C))\circ b_{O,\mathcal LC}:\widehat O\mathcal LC\longrightarrow\mathcal LOC.$$
These maps are natural isomorphisms on the stated domain. For every whole-system derived morphism $\phi:C\to D$,
$$r_{O,D}\circ\widehat O(\mathcal L\phi)=\mathcal L(O\phi)\circ r_{O,C}.$$
For a finite composable word $w=O_m\cdots O_1$, the iterated $r$ gives a natural isomorphism $r_{w,C}:\widehat w\mathcal LC\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LwC$. It agrees with substitution of the entire-system counit at every intermediate object, independently of parenthesization; explicitly
$$r_{vw,C}=r_{v,wC}\circ\widehat v(r_{w,C}).$$
For a whole-system comparison $t:w\Rightarrow w'$ built from the specified finite pullback compositor, scalar/pullback comparison, scalar associator and action unitors, its counit-built completed comparison is
$$\widehat t_{\mathcal LC}=r_{w',C}^{-1}\circ\mathcal L(t_C)\circ r_{w,C}.$$
Thus this identification also holds after whiskering by any further completed operation and for composites of these maps; it holds for morphisms of entire derived quotient diagrams, including inverses, rather than merely after finite evaluation.

For coefficient scalar associativity and units, the same identification is compatible with the completion maps $\chi_{L/E,K}:K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat S_{L/E}K$ with quotient/zero-shifted-product normalization [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. In particular, if $\alpha^\otimes:(K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_L)\otimes^L_{R_L}R_M\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes^L_{R_E}R_M$ is the ordinary derived tensor associator, realization of the system scalar associator is exactly
$$\chi_{M/E,K}\circ\alpha^\otimes_K\circ(\chi_{L/E,K}^{-1}\otimes^L1)\circ\chi_{M/L,\widehat S_{L/E}K}^{-1}.$$
For $E=L$, realization of the system multiplication unit is the multiplication/completeness identification $\widehat S_{E/E}K\cong K$. No faithfulness of separate finite reduction functors and no finite Tor-amplitude assumption is asserted or needed.

proof.text: First identify the actual counit, rather than choose level isomorphisms. The system adjunction gives a natural map $e_C:\mathcal R\mathcal LC\to C$ whose evaluations are the scalar-extension adjuncts of the total-limit projections. For a normalized $C$, DVR effectivity says precisely that these canonical maps $(\mathcal LC)\otimes^L A_{F,n}\to C_n$ are coherent isomorphisms. Derived evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms in the system category, so $e_C$ itself is an isomorphism there. This argument applies without a cohomological or Tor bound. The model definition fixes its underlying constant-tower counit to the K-injective ordinary limit cone, so it is the $e$ specified in the item.

proof.text: The supplied primitive model $b_{O,K}$ is a natural isomorphism. Since a functor takes an inverse to an inverse, $\mathcal L O(e_C)$ is an isomorphism by step 1; their composite is $r_{O,C}$. The word construction stays on normalized systems: write $K=\mathcal LC$ and use $O(e_C):O\mathcal RK\xrightarrow{\sim}OC$. The effective-model statement gives normalization of $O\mathcal RK$ for each primitive operation; normalization is invariant under a system isomorphism, by conjugating its transition-adjoint squares. Thus $OC$ is normalized. Repeat this at each intermediate system. The stipulated constructible-complete intermediate realizations are exactly the domain restriction needed to apply the effective-model statement at the next stage.

proof.text: For $\phi:C\to D$, naturality of $b$ gives $b_{O,\mathcal LD}\widehat O(\mathcal L\phi)=\mathcal LO\mathcal R(\mathcal L\phi)b_{O,\mathcal LC}$. Naturality of the adjunction counit gives $e_D\mathcal R\mathcal L\phi=\phi e_C$ in the entire derived system category. Apply the functor $\mathcal LO$ to the latter equality and substitute it in the former. This gives $r_{O,D}\widehat O(\mathcal L\phi)=\mathcal L(O\phi)r_{O,C}$. Both naturalities concern arbitrary derived-system morphisms, so the calculation applies to inverses as well.

proof.text: Define $r_{1,C}=1_{\mathcal LC}$ for the empty word, and recursively $r_{Ow,C}=r_{O,wC}\widehat O(r_{w,C})$. Step 3 proves its naturality by induction on length; step 2 proves invertibility. To check parentheses, expand three consecutive blocks: both $r_{(uv)w,C}$ and $r_{u(vw),C}$ are $r_{u,vwC}\widehat u(r_{v,wC})\widehat u\widehat v(r_{w,C})$. This uses only associativity of composition and functoriality. Induction on the lengths of the blocks proves $r_{vw,C}=r_{v,wC}\widehat v(r_{w,C})$ for every cut of a word, including empty blocks.

proof.text: This recursion is the promised whole-counit substitution, with no additional comparison chosen. For two primitive letters $A,B$, expand it as $\mathcal LA(e_{BC})b_{A,\mathcal LBC}\widehat A(\mathcal LB(e_C))\widehat A(b_{B,\mathcal LC})$. Naturality of $b_A$ moves $\widehat A(\mathcal LB(e_C))$ across $b_A$; the resulting system maps contain $e_{BC}\mathcal R\mathcal LB(e_C)$. Counit naturality identifies this with $B(e_C)e_{B\mathcal R\mathcal LC}$. This is exactly substituting the original whole-system counit before the next operation. Iterate the same equality for each additional letter. The unit/counit triangle identities cancel an inserted reduction-realization unit. All equalities used here belong to the system adjunction, prior to realization.

proof.text: For a specified system comparison $t:w\Rightarrow w'$, identify the completed source and target with $\mathcal LwC$ and $\mathcal Lw'C$ by step 5. In these identifications its construction is $\mathcal L(t_C)$: the finite pullback compositor, scalar/pullback comparison, scalar associator and unit maps are the fixed maps of entire quotient diagrams, and the completed construction substitutes the whole counits at the intervening objects. Undoing the two identifications gives $\widehat t_{\mathcal LC}=r_{w',C}^{-1}\mathcal L(t_C)r_{w,C}$. This also specifies what is meant by its counit-built completed comparison; it does not identify an arbitrary completed isomorphism with that comparison. In a composite $s\circ t$ the middle factors $r_{w',C}r_{w',C}^{-1}$ cancel; for $t^{-1}$ invert the formula. Thus the claimed formula holds for composites and inverses.

proof.text: For left whiskering by a primitive $A$, use step 3 with the system arrow $t_C:wC\to w'C$. It gives $r_{A,w'C}\widehat A(\mathcal L(t_C))=\mathcal L(A(t_C))r_{A,wC}$. Combine this with the formula in step 6 and the recursion for $r_{Aw}$: the resulting completed comparison is $\widehat A(\widehat t_{\mathcal LC})$. For right whiskering by a primitive $B$, the same formula evaluated at $BC$, conjugated by $\widehat w(r_{B,C})$ and $\widehat w'(r_{B,C})$, is the completed comparison at $\widehat B\mathcal LC$; naturality of the completed comparison in the isomorphism $r_{B,C}$ gives precisely this square. Induction gives both assertions for arbitrary further words. No inference from equality of separate evaluations is used.

proof.text: It remains to fix the scalar normalization. Put $K=\mathcal LC$, $R=R_E$, $S=R_L$, $T=R_M$, and let $\beta_K$ be the scalar associator obtained in step 6. Set $d_K=\chi_{M/L,\widehat S_{L/E}K}\circ(\chi_{L/E,K}\otimes^L1_T)$, from $(K\otimes_R^LS)\otimes_S^LT$ to $\widehat S_{M/L}\widehat S_{L/E}K$. The finite-free comparison says each $\chi$ here is an isomorphism and that $K\otimes_R^LS$ is complete. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to K$. Changing rings preserves K-flatness and flat terms, so $P\otimes_R S$ and $(P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S T$ compute successive scalar extensions; the canonical comparisons respect replacement. The prescribed scalar model and the scalar-comparison descent statement identify each initial $\chi$ with the chain map having the actual quotient maps in its unshifted Roos product and zero in its shifted product. These specify actual chain maps, not only evaluated derived morphisms.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemma 3.5.7, pp. 22,24-26; agent expansion of the normalized scalar comparison, with the whole-counit model of Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: Compute the whole-system adjuncts of $\beta_Kd_K$ and $\chi_{M/E,K}\alpha^\otimes_K$, after identifying their target $\widehat S_{M/E}K$ with $\mathcal LS_{M/E}\mathcal RK$ by its model. The cone-counit identity $\epsilon_Q\Delta(r_\theta)=\theta^\Delta$ turns each zero-shifted-product quotient lift into its original strict compatible quotient family. Extension/restriction counits then act by multiplication. In the nested expression the scalar associator sends $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes ab$; in the direct expression ordinary tensor reassociation followed by the quotient map has exactly the same value. More explicitly, the level-$n$ adjunct on a generator $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$, with $a\in S$, $b\in T$, $c\in A_{M,n}$, is $x\otimes(\bar a\bar b c)$ in both expressions. The maps commute with quotient transitions because reduction preserves multiplication, and with site restrictions because multiplication is a sheaf operation. Balancing gives equality on all tensors, degree by degree; scalar coefficients have degree zero, so the maps commute with the cochain differential. This proves equality of the strict whole-diagram maps computing the adjuncts, with their quotient transitions retained.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemma 3.5.7, pp. 22,24-26; agent expansion of the normalized scalar comparison, with the whole-counit model of Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: Localize the strict equality of step 9, retaining the normalized model comparisons. The descent assertion for $\chi$ and the supplied natural model normalizations permit every flat-term K-flat representative, so the result is independent of $P$. The adjunction $\mathcal R_M\dashv\mathcal L_M$ is a bijection on Hom sets into $\mathcal LS_{M/E}\mathcal R_EK$; equality of its entire-system adjuncts therefore gives $\beta_Kd_K=\chi_{M/E,K}\alpha^\otimes_K$. For the original system $C$, use the isomorphism $e_C:\mathcal R_EK\to C$ of step 1. Naturality of the system scalar associator, of $r$ (step 3), and of $\chi$ carries the just computed square to $C$; the factors $e_C$ cancel. Invert $d_K$ using step 8. In order, its inverse is $(\chi_{L/E,K}^{-1}\otimes^L1)\chi_{M/L,\widehat S_{L/E}K}^{-1}$, giving exactly the displayed conjugated tensor-associator formula. This uses faithfulness of a single adjunction Hom bijection, never faithfulness of finite reduction functors.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemma 3.5.7, pp. 22,24-26; agent expansion of the normalized scalar comparison, with the whole-counit model of Stacks Tag 0941.

proof.text: When $L=E$, the same computation uses the system unitor $s\otimes x\mapsto sx$. The scalar-comparison descent statement identifies its initial lift with the quotient unit of $P$ having zero shifted-product component. The finite-free comparison identifies $\chi_{E/E,K}$, after $K\otimes_R^LR\cong K$, with the natural completeness isomorphism $K\to\mathcal L\mathcal RK$. Hence the counit-built map $\widehat S_{E/E}K\to K$ is its inverse followed by multiplication, as asserted. This also covers equalities among $E,L,M$ in the associator formula. Every scalar coefficient extension used in steps 8-11 is the finite-free completed-ring extension; no flatness of a finite quotient-ring map and no finite Tor-amplitude were used.
